_README: A budget is the most wire bytes one REQUEST (path plus query) may serve. Request identity is (path, query), so one route may carry several entries.

Two enforcement points read this table: the pre-merge fleet sweep (dashboard/tests/test_payload_budget_sweep.py) and the live predicate (dashboard/src/dashboard/payload_check.py, run daily by the dashboard-payload-budgets recurrence chain).

history is APPEND-ONLY. The effective budget is the last entry. To raise or lower a budget, APPEND {budget_bytes, task, reason}; never edit, reorder or delete a recorded entry. The base-relative test in dashboard/tests/test_payload_budgets.py refuses it.
Headroom convention for a new number over a fresh live measurement m: round max(1.25*m, m + 16384) up to 2 significant figures.

Slack rule (payload_budgets.MAX_SLACK_RATIO, payload_budgets.SLACK_FLOOR_BYTES): the sweep fails when a budget exceeds max(MAX_SLACK_RATIO * measured, measured + SLACK_FLOOR_BYTES), so a real shrink must be recorded as a lowered entry and a fixture that stops reaching its data turns red.

data_keyed_maps lists the key paths of dicts keyed by DATA (project labels, dates, task ids) rather than by field name. Each is a list of segments, with [] for list descent and {} for a collapsed map. Field accounting collapses their keys to {}.
exempt is for TEMPLATED routes only, each with a reason. Entry paths plus exempt paths must equal every GET route under /api/v2/dashboard/.
The synthetic fleet the sweep measures lives in dashboard/tests/_payload_fleet.py (its census) and dashboard/tests/_payload_fleet_seed.py (its on-disk seeders).
